newsitem.title: USA: ConAgra declines comment on WSJ story.
newsitem.headline: ConAgra declines comment on WSJ story.

text.p: ConAgra declined to comment Thursday on a Wall Street Journal report that said it had agreed to pay millions of dollars in penalties to settle a criminal inquiry into its Peavey Grain unit's practice of spraying water on stored grain.
"We really can't comment until it is final," a ConAgra spokesowman told Reuters in a telephone interview from the company's headquarters in Omaha, Neb.
The paper quoted people familiar with the probe as saying that the Justice Department was also seeking charges against some former Peavey employees.

The report said the Justice Department had planned to announce details of the penalties at a news conference Thursday in Indianopolis, but that the announcement was postponed because of hitches in the agreeement's wording.
ConAgra's spokeswoman said that although she did not know when the news conference would be held, she believed it would happen "sooner rather than later."
Oficials at the U.S. Attorney's Offfice in Indianapolis were not immediately available to comment on the case.
